# SOP Audit & Build Plan – The Forge Belfast

## **Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member Onboarding** – no documented first-contact-to-first-class journey; inconsistent induction, fitness assessment capture, goal-setting

- **Complaints & Incident Log** – no formal capture, investigation, or follow-up; health & safety blind spot

# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

**1. Start with your actual revenue first, not theory**
Pull your last 3 months of transactions. What are members *actually* paying for right now? Group by: group classes, personal training, nutrition coaching, challenges, retail. This is your real menu — now you just need to organize and price it honestly.

**2. Split it into two different documents immediately**
- **Coaches version**: What they can *sell* + commission structure + upsell triggers (e.g., "if member asks about X, offer Y"). Make it scannable in 2 minutes.
- **Members version**: What they *get* + pricing + results promise + what's NOT included (kills scope creep). This goes on your website and printed at reception.

**3. Ruthlessly define "included" to stop scope creep NOW**
For each offering, write: "This package includes [X sessions/features]. It does NOT include [Y]." Example: "Unlimited classes includes group fitness — not 1-on-1 form checks outside class time." This prevents coaches from giving away premium services and protects your margins.

**4. Price in tiers, not à la carte**
Don't list individual services. Create 3-4 membership tiers (e.g., Foundation/Power/Elite) so members trade UP, not sideways. Price the top tier so aggressively that mid-tier feels like the obvious choice.

**5. Get this to coaches within 48 hours for feedback**
They'll spot what's missing or unworkable. One round of coach input = prevents rebuilding this in 3 months when reality hits.

# The Forge — Fractional CFO Audit & Action Plan

## REVENUE — URGENT PRIORITY

• **Churn spike in May (12.8%) is your leak.** Last 3 months (Jun–Aug) average 5.7% churn; May was double that and killed £1,800+ in recurring revenue. Root cause: investigate member feedback, class cancellations, or staff changes in May. Fix retention *now* — it's cheaper than acquisition.

• **Rev/member collapsed in August to £103 (down from £145 in July).** You grew headcount to 157 but revenue fell to £16,160. Members are paying *less* or attending fewer paid sessions. Audit your pricing tiers: are new members on legacy plans? Are dropins/class cards being discounted? Enforce price consistency — even a £5/month average uplift across 157 members = +£785/month.

• **Add paid upsells immediately.** Current model is memberships + cards only. Launch: PT sessions (£35–50/hour), nutrition plans (£25–40/month), small-group challenges (£15 entry). Target: £1,500/month from add-ons by end of Q4 2026. Women's fitness = high attach rate.

• **Peak hours filling; off-peak (6am, 9–10am weekdays, 2–4pm) are still soft.** Offer "Quieter Hour" 20% discount or free class-pass upgrades for off-peak bookings. Convert 20 quiet slots/week = +£200–300/month.

---

## EXPENSES — SECOND PRIORITY

• **Cash burn in Aug (–£5,335 net) after a profitable Jul (+£8,092) flags cost control drift.** Compare Jul & Aug payroll, utilities, supplies: something spiked. Audit supplier invoices for one-offs (new kit, repairs) and confirm staffing didn't creep. Target: cash neutral or +£2k/month minimum.

• **Rent + utilities likely 35–40% of your £16k monthly revenue (estimate: £5,600–6,400).** Post-relocation, confirm the new space rent/rates are locked in fixed-term and didn't inflate vs. the old studio. If rent rose >10%, model break-even headcount — you may need 165+ active to justify it.

• **Payroll is probably your largest variable cost.** With 157 members, you likely run 2–3 instructors + 1 PT + admin. Benchmark: payroll should be ≤45% of revenue
